title: Doctoral (PhD) student position in developmental neuroscience
employment: Full-time doctoral studentship, up to 4 years
description: Eric Herlenius' group studies how brainstem neural networks, inflammation and developmental transitions shape cardiorespiratory control in newborns and children. The project combines rodent models with single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, with a central focus on computational integration of complex multimodal datasets and gene-regulatory programs.
match_reasons: Direct overlap with single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics
Strong R/Python, Linux, sequencing and bioinformatics workflow fit
Relevant wet-lab background in cell culture, molecular biology and imaging
Current KI/SciLifeLab research experience and scientific publication record
gaps: Deep-learning experience is foundational rather than extensive
headline: Bioinformatics & Molecular Biology Researcher | Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics
statement: Interdisciplinary researcher combining bioinformatics, genomics and molecular biology, with hands-on experience in sequencing workflows, cell culture and translational research. I use R, Python, Linux and reproducible pipelines to analyze high-dimensional biological data, including single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics, and I am motivated to investigate how gene-regulatory programs and tissue context shape developmental disease mechanisms.

title: Doctoral student in computational pathology and medical artificial intelligence
location_detail: Department of Medical Epidemiology and Biostatistics, Solna
employment: Full-time doctoral studentship, up to 4 years
description: Kimmo Kartasalo's DDLS/SciLifeLab-affiliated group develops large-scale image-analysis and deep-learning methods for precision cancer medicine. The doctoral project evaluates and develops foundation models and agentic AI for prostate-cancer diagnosis, grading and prognosis across patient populations and pathology platforms, including multimodal integration of tissue images, molecular data and clinical variables.
match_reasons: Eligible biotechnology/bioinformatics academic background
Strong Python, scientific programming, version control and reproducibility
Cancer biology, microscopy and multimodal omics experience are relevant
Demonstrated scientific writing through publications and theses
gaps: No documented digital pathology or whole-slide-image work
PyTorch/deep-learning experience is not yet demonstrated at production or research depth
headline: Computational Biology Researcher | Cancer Biology, Genomics and Reproducible Analysis
statement: Interdisciplinary researcher with a foundation in bioinformatics, cancer biology and molecular biotechnology, combining Python/R analysis with experimental work and scientific communication. My experience includes tumor models, microscopy, sequencing data, reproducible workflows and multimodal transcriptomics; I am motivated to deepen my expertise in machine learning and medical image analysis for clinically useful precision-oncology tools.

title: Project Coordinator for Large Research Study on Human intestinal diseases
description: Eduardo Villablanca's mucosal-immunology team is coordinating a three-lab translational study of inflammatory bowel disease and mucosal healing. The role combines project coordination, ethical and regulatory documentation, human-sample biobanking, single-cell suspension and organoid work, meeting facilitation, and communication of results across KI and SciLifeLab laboratories.
match_reasons: Direct hands-on organoid, cell-culture and molecular-biology experience
Strong single-cell/spatial biology awareness and SciLifeLab familiarity
Track record of independent multidisciplinary research and presentations
Well matched to coordination across wet-lab and computational teams
gaps: Swedish biobank administration is not documented
Formal multi-lab project-management responsibility is not explicit in the master CV
headline: Biomedical Researcher | Organoid Models, Single-Cell Biology and Project Coordination
statement: Biomedical researcher experienced in organoid and 2D/3D cell culture, molecular-biology workflows, translational cancer models and cross-disciplinary work at KTH, Karolinska Institutet and SciLifeLab. I combine meticulous experimental practice with bioinformatics literacy, scientific reporting and an independent, structured working style suited to coordinating samples, documentation, timelines and communication across collaborative research teams.

title: Biomedical systems developer to CLINTEC
location_detail: CLINTEC, Division of Ear, Nose and Throat Diseases
employment: Full-time permanent position; six-month trial period
description: Mikael Benson's medical-digital-twins group develops computational methods to identify cancer disease mechanisms, biomarkers and drug targets. The role applies machine learning and statistical methods to single-cell and spatial data, evaluates candidate targets, supports publications and presentations, and collaborates across Swedish and international EU projects.
match_reasons: Computational-science Master's-level profile with bioinformatics specialization
Relevant single-cell and spatial transcriptomics project experience
Cancer, biomarker and translational-research background
Strong scientific writing and interdisciplinary collaboration record
gaps: Advert asks for experience with single-cell analyses including spatial; the CV shows project work but depth should be evidenced in application answers
headline: Biomedical Systems & Bioinformatics Researcher | Single-Cell, Spatial and Cancer Biology
statement: Interdisciplinary biomedical researcher combining bioinformatics, genomics and cancer biology with hands-on wet-lab experience. I develop reproducible R/Python workflows for sequencing and transcriptomic data, including single-cell and spatial analyses, and connect computational results to disease mechanisms, biomarkers and translational questions through experience at Karolinska Institutet, KTH and SciLifeLab.

title: Doctoral (PhD) student position in spatial proteomics of mitochondrial disease
location_detail: Department of Medical Biochemistry and Biophysics, Biomedicum
employment: Full-time doctoral studentship, up to 4 years
description: Develop spatial single-cell proteomics with Deep Visual Proteomics, high-content imaging, AI-guided segmentation, laser microdissection and mass spectrometry to resolve mitochondrial-disease trajectories in mouse tissue.
match_reasons: Required molecular-biology, histology, (immuno)staining and Python backgrounds are documented
Direct fit to spatial biology, imaging, cell/cancer models and interdisciplinary wet-/dry-lab work
Git/GitHub, reproducible workflows and KI/SciLifeLab collaboration are explicit in the CV
Publications and technical presentations demonstrate research output and communication
gaps: No documented mass-spectrometry-based proteomics or Deep Visual Proteomics
Deep-learning image-analysis experience is foundational rather than extensive
No stated mouse-model or mitochondrial-disease specialization
headline: Interdisciplinary Biomedical Researcher | Spatial Biology, Imaging & Bioinformatics
statement: Interdisciplinary biomedical researcher combining molecular biology, histology and immunostaining with Python-based bioinformatics and reproducible workflows. I bring hands-on experience in cell culture, cancer models, microscopy and spatial transcriptomics, and am motivated to connect image-based phenotypes to multimodal biological data in mitochondrial disease.

title: Doctoral (PhD) student position in spatial transcriptomics, bioinformatics, and cancer immunology (DDLS PhD program)
employment: Full-time doctoral studentship, up to 4 years
description: Use and develop tools to integrate multimodal spatial data, map B- and T-cell clones and their tissue niches, and study cancer-associated immune responses within the DDLS PhD program.
match_reasons: The advert specifically seeks spatial transcriptomics, bioinformatics, biology, Python and R; all are documented
Cancer biology and tumor-on-a-chip research provide relevant translational context
Long-read sequencing, structural-variant analysis and single-cell/spatial projects support modality integration
KI/SciLifeLab research experience, publications and presentations support research readiness
gaps: No documented high-resolution spatial VDJ/transcriptomics or immune-clone analysis
Immunology is relevant but not a primary documented specialization
headline: Spatial Transcriptomics & Bioinformatics Researcher | Cancer Immunology
statement: Interdisciplinary bioinformatics and molecular-biology researcher with direct experience in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, tumor models and sequencing-data analysis. I use Python, R, Linux and reproducible workflows to translate complex biological questions into rigorous, collaborative analyses, and I am eager to contribute to data-driven spatial immune-niche research in cancer.

title: PhD student in Bioinformatics (protein-structure evolution)
location_detail: Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics, Frescati
employment: Full-time doctoral studentship, up to 4 years
description: Combine large-scale protein-structure datasets, deep-learning-based structural embeddings and comparative genomics to analyze domain divergence, novel domain architectures and protein-structure evolution.
match_reasons: Master's-level molecular-biology/biotechnology and bioinformatics background meets advertised entry requirements
AlphaFold familiarity, sequence analysis, Python, R and bioinformatics workflows are relevant to the project
Genomics, structural-variant analysis and HPC experience support large-scale computational work
Research output, thesis work and scientific presentations support doctoral research readiness
gaps: Fewer deep-learning and protein-structure-modelling depth are documented compared with the advert's core methods
No documented protein-evolution or structural-embedding research experience
headline: Bioinformatics Researcher | Protein Structure, Genomics & Reproducible Computation
statement: Interdisciplinary bioinformatics and molecular-biology researcher with experience in sequencing analysis, genomics, structural-variant discovery and reproducible Python/R/HPC workflows. I bring foundational familiarity with AlphaFold and molecular-structure analysis alongside a strong translational-biology base, and am motivated to deepen my expertise in protein-structure informatics and evolution.

title: Research assistant in bioinformatics applied to machine learning in regulatory genomics
location_detail: Department of Cell and Molecular Biology, Biomedicum, Solna
description: Join the Llorens laboratory to analyze single-cell and spatial multiome datasets from mouse models and human patient samples, study gene regulation in CNS injury and repair, support deep-learning models for gene-therapy constructs, and connect computational predictions with genomics validation.
match_reasons: The MSc bioinformatics/biotechnology profile directly meets the stated degree requirement
Single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, R, Python and reproducible sequencing workflows are documented in the CV

Cell culture, molecular biology and translational research experience support collaboration with experimental researchers
gaps: No documented scATAC-seq, multiome or enhancer-biology analysis
Machine-learning and deep-learning experience is foundational rather than extensive
No stated CNS injury, repair or gene-therapy specialization
contact: Enric Llorens — enric.llorens@ki.se; Margherita Zamboni — margherita.zamboni@ki.se
headline: Bioinformatics Researcher | Single-Cell, Spatial Genomics & Molecular Biology
statement: Interdisciplinary bioinformatics and molecular-biology researcher with hands-on experience in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, sequencing workflows, cell culture and translational research. I use Python, R, Linux and HPC-based reproducible workflows to analyze high-dimensional biological data, and am motivated to connect gene-regulatory insights with experimental genomics and CNS repair research.
